html:
SMTO-CAP-0001 — This Task isn't allowed to use that tool or program

GUID: a6abb320-6db7-4337-b390-26f6891b0870
Slug: capability-excluded
Domain: CAP · Subsystem: cap

What happened

  • The Task tried to use a tool, Skill or program that your capability settings block, so SMTO stopped that step and didn't run it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Capabilities next to the message box. Use the Apply to list to check This prompt, This conversation and Global for the item set to Never or − (Exclude). Any of these levels can block it, and a prompt or conversation setting overrides Global.
  2. Change it to Auto, or to ○ (Enable, or Default for a shell program), select Apply, then send your request again as a new message. Tasks already accepted keep the settings they started with, so only new work uses the change.
  3. If you want to keep it blocked, ask for the job in simpler steps that don't need that program. While any program is blocked, SMTO also refuses commands too complex to check for it.

What success looks like

  • The new Task runs the step, and its activity shows the tool or command running instead of being blocked.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; your Global capability settings may be managed for you. Don't keep resending the same request unchanged; it will be blocked the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The run's active capability policy excludes the requested tool, Skill or shell executable, or a shell command could not be proven to avoid excluded executables, so the step was refused before dispatch.

What this means

  • The active capability selection excludes the tool or executable, or shell inspection cannot prove compliance with those exclusions. Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.

Why this can happen

  • The active capability selection excludes the tool or executable, or shell inspection cannot prove compliance with those exclusions.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare selected capabilities and executable exclusions with the actual command structure; distinguish exclusion from unavailable installation.

How to fix it

  • Check native_capability_policy (excluded_tool_ids, excluded_skill_ids, enabled_skill_ids, excluded_shell_executables) at the prompt, conversation and global scopes; remove the exclusion and start new work (accepted and queued tasks keep their snapshot), or keep it and use an advertised capability. While any shell executable is excluded, commands whose executables cannot be determined statically are refused as well.
  • Use an advertised capability or start a new task with the intended capability selection.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended action is advertised and satisfies the task's exclusions before dispatch.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
